name: The Human-AI Sandwich
description: The Human does the first 10% - framing the problemThe AI does the middle 80% - the heavy liftingThe Human does the last 10% - final review and edits
example: Never submit something that you haven't read entirely. Let's avoid AI-slop.

name: The Parts of a Prompt
description: Define a clear objective, provide context, offer motivation, explain the audience, give instructions, and specify the output format.
example: "You are an experienced product strategist. Summarize these meeting notes into actionable insights for non-technical executives. Output a concise bullet list focused on product and revenue topics, exclude HR, keep it under 200 words, and include action owner per bullet."

name: Let AI Become a Natural Partner
description: Like you would reach for your phone to check for directions, you should reach for AI for anything related to Writing, Reasoning, Research, and Analysis.
example:
Using Voice Mode or Voice to Text can make AI feel more organic.
Start AI chats immediately on your phone/watch, then continue them later from your computer.

name: AI as Skill Multiplier
description: AI is better at expanding your existing capabilities than giving you completely new ones. Knowing what is possible and recognizing good outputs will help you to leverage AI effectively.
example: You can ask, "Write me a sales script". But if you cannot tell good from bad yourself, then the output is uncertain.

name: AI Skills Compound
description: The more tools and techniques you know, the more creative you can be - and the more you will learn over time.
example:
Help me research a complex topic.
Draft a presentation outline.
Generate images to go along the main sections.
Create the presentation using HTML or PowerPoint.

name: Upload Files
description: Provide original files (PDFs, CSVs, docs) so the model can pull details directly when needed.
example: "I've uploaded a 40-page research PDF. Use it as your only source to summarize the main findings in a one-page brief."

name: Context Formats
description: Share the same context in different forms — text, screenshots, pasted tables — to improve understanding.
example: "Here's my spreadsheet pasted as text, and here is a screenshot of the first few rows to help you understand the structure."

name: Lots of Context
description: When unsure what's needed, err on the side of giving more raw material: notes, transcripts, webpage dumps, screenshots.
example: "Here are my messy project notes and meeting transcripts. Please extract the main decisions, open questions, and owner for each action item."

name: Prune Irrelevant Information
description: Remove obviously unrelated content so the model isn't distracted or misled by noise.
example:
Remove unnecessary text/data that don't contribute to the current task.
Start a new chat when changing topics, or when there is too many distractions in the current conversation.

name: Structure Context
description: Organize inputs into labeled sections.
example:
"GOAL: propose a launch plan for the next 30 days.
BACKGROUND: […]
CONSTRAINTS: […]
EXAMPLES: […]

name: Pre-Process with AI
description: First ask the model to summarize or reorganize large, messy inputs into compact, structured notes.
example:
"Summarize these 20 pages into a concise outline."
Then, "Turn that outline into a 2-page strategy memo."

name: Define Output Structure
description: Describe the exact fields and columns you want the model to return.
example: "Return a markdown table with these columns: 'Feature', 'User Segment', 'Value Proposition', 'Risk Level (Low/Med/High)'."

name: Provide Examples
description: Show a model answer and tell the AI to follow that style and structure. Note: The model can sometimes copy examples too closely.
example: "Here is an example performance review paragraph. Using this style and tone, write a review for an engineer with the following achievements: …"

name: Break into Sub-Steps
description: Decompose big tasks into smaller, manageable steps.
example:
Prompt 1: "Create an outline for a 10-slide pitch deck."
Prompt 2: "Write the voice track for slide 1."
Prompt 3: "Write the speaker notes for slide 1."

name: Iterate
description: Run iterative cycles: draft → refine → repeat until satisfied.
example:
Prompt 1: "Draft a 1-page proposal."
Prompt 2: "Rewrite it to be 20% shorter and more persuasive."

name: Self-Iterate
description: Have the model critique its own output and propose improvements.
example: "1) Identify the weaknesses and missing details of your last response. 2) Rewrite incorporating your own feedback."

name: Draft in a Canvas
description: Use a dedicated drafting space for long-form content to make editing easier.
example: "Write a detailed project plan in a pop-out canvas, including sections for Objectives, Scope, Timeline, and Risks."

name: "Think Very Long and Hard"
description: Adding this phrase triggers extra computation on reasoning models. Use it for complex problems that require deep logical analysis.
example: "Think very long and hard and design an algorithm to allocate budget across channels under these constraints and justify your approach."

name: Ask for Assumptions
description: Require the model to explain its assumptions, reasoning steps, and approach before answering.
example:
Prompt 1: "Don't answer yet. First, explain your assumptions and the method you'll use."
Prompt 2: "A better interest rate to use is 8%, and assume the interest is applied monthly. Now tell me the answer."

name: Request Multiple Options
description: Have the model generate several options with pros and cons so you can choose.
example: "Give me 3 different positioning statements for this product, with pros and cons for each and a recommendation."

name: Trigger Self-Critique
description: Ask the model to play devil's advocate and challenge its own conclusions.
example: "You just recommended Option B. Now play devil's advocate and argue why Option B might fail and what we should watch for."

name: Show Its Work
description: Instruct the model to think through the problem step-by-step before responding. Especially important for non-reasoning models.
example: "Talk through your reasoning step by step before giving a final answer: Is this A/B test design statistically sound?"

name: Use a Thinking Model
description: Use a reasoning-focused model when accuracy and logical depth matter most.
example: "Analyze this legal clause for ambiguities and outline possible interpretations and risks."

name: Use an Instant Model
description: Use a faster model for bulk, repetitive, or low-risk tasks.
example: "Convert this unstructured log of customer complaints into a 1000-row table with columns for 'Customer', 'Issue Category', and 'Sentiment'."

name: Structure Data
description: AI can turn unstructured text into structured formats like tables or JSON.
example: "Turn the text of this web page into a markdown table with the following headers: Product Name, Price, & Description."

name: Reformat Data
description: AI can intelligently refactor or reformat data to your specifications.
example: "Take all of the names and put them into Lastname, Firstname format."

name: Internal Analysis
description: Using Python, AI can run calculations or generate figures and visualizations.
example: "Using our historic growth data, project when we will double in size. Plot our projected growth curve over the historic data."

name: External Analysis
description: AI can help you run analyses by generating Excel or Google Sheet formulas.
example: "Help me develop an Excel formula that will calculate the correlation coefficient between sales commission percentage and closing rate."

name: Internal Capabilities
description: Using Python, AI can do simple actions: generate QR codes, convert image types, add headers to PDFs, etc.
example: "Combine these two PDFs and add page numbers to the bottom right in Arial 12pt font."

name: Debugging & Troubleshooting
description: AI can walk you through complex problems if you upload screenshots, pictures, or error codes.
example: "Here is a screenshot of my computer. Where did the menu bar go, and how do I get it back?"

name: Turn Chats into Reusable Prompts
description: Convert successful conversations into general, reusable prompts. Ask the AI: "Analyze this conversation and draft a reusable prompt that would recreate this kind of output for any topic."

name: Parameterize Your Prompts
description: Add variables like {{Audience}}, {{Tone}}, and {{Length}} so prompts can be reused easily across different contexts.

name: Organize a Prompt Library
description: Maintain a catalog of your best prompts by use case and domain. Build institutional knowledge over time.

name: Beware of Hallucinations
description: AI models can confidently produce incorrect information, including invented facts, fake citations, non-existent URLs, or fabricated statistics. More advanced models include techniques to reduce this behavior, so risk varies by model, but human judgment remains essential.
example: With experience, you'll get better at recognizing where hallucinations are most likely and when extra scrutiny is needed.

name: Require Checkable Sources
description: Ask the AI to provide verifiable sources for factual claims. Note: Always check them - sources can be hallucinated.

name: Have the AI Check for Errors
description: Ask the model to check its own answers for accuracy. Reasoning models often do this automatically with "Think very long and hard."

name: Sanity-Check Math
description: Double-check all numerical and statistical output, especially when the model is not in reasoning mode.

name: Validate Data Inputs
description: Confirm that inputs are accurate and well-parsed, especially from PDFs and images.

name: Clear Chat History
description: AI can be biased by prior chat history. Start a new chat if quality seems to be decreasing.

name: Avoid Plagiarism
description: AI may mimic phrasing from training data. Always edit, add original thinking, and run checks where required.

name: Remove Sensitive Data
description: Avoid including personal, confidential, or regulated information unless you're in a compliant setup.

name: Disclose AI Assistance
description: Be transparent about AI involvement where compliance, ethics, or expectations require it.

name: Don't Delegate High-Risk Decisions
description: Use AI for analysis and options, not final calls in legal, medical, financial, or HR decisions.
